caption: We pay R9 400 for a house and R1 900 for Friday chicken. Which one surprises you more?

slides.title:
What our bond
really costs us
on R38 200 p/m
Living in Bela-Bela
slides.body:
Him 35, her 32
Married, two kids (4 and 1)
Jobs: Lodge maintenance supervisor & clinic nursing assistant
Household net income: R38 200 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.includes: 3 bedroom house, bond over 20 years, home insurance, levies
slides.body: Nobody told us the bond is just the start. The geyser, the roof and the boundary wall are all ours now.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Family shop, formula, nappies, school lunches
slides.body: A tin of formula lasts six days. I do not want to say what that adds up to.

slides.title: Cars and petrol
slides.includes: One Corsa Utility instalment, petrol for two commutes
slides.body: We need two cars because the clinic and the lodge are in opposite directions.

slides.title: Childcare
slides.includes: Crèche for the baby, Grade R fees and transport
slides.body: My wife's salary almost pays for it. We both know that and neither of us says it.

slides.title: Takeaways
slides.includes: Friday chicken, Sunday pizza, the odd Mugg & Bean
slides.body: Friday takeaways started as a treat. Now it is a tradition we pay R1 900 for.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: electricity & water, hospital plan, black tax, funeral policies, stokvel, phones
slides.body: Six line items, R9 440. The hospital plan is the one we argue about, and the one I would not drop.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R38 200. It looks healthy until the geyser goes. It went in July.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
We uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction.

The takeaways were bigger than the baby's formula.

No bank login needed.
